key_idea: The 'both or neither' rule forces a team to be an entire weakly connected component, so just count components of size k that are complete mutual cliques.
sketch: Union endpoints of every directed entry with DSU. For each component count vertices and directed edges; it is a valid team iff size == k and edge count == k(k-1) (entries are unique, so that many edges means every ordered pair is present). The answer is the number of such components; with k = 1 it is the number of isolated vertices. Complexity O((n+m) alpha). Pitfalls: k(k-1) needs 64 bits, and no binomial counting is needed since a team cannot be a strict subset of a component.
